text:
nisha: Quick follow-up to the canary/fallback RFC. Proposing a lightweight policy arbiter that ranks fallback actions probabilistically to reduce synchronized flips across tenants. Thoughts?

tom: Interesting. How does probabilistic help us vs strict thresholds?

nisha: If detectors are noisy across many services, strict thresholds can cause mass rollbacks at once. Probabilistic selection (weighted by policy_score and recent-change-risk) spaces out actions and reduces load spikes.

eli: Need to make sure this doesn't reduce safety. If model quality drops severe, we still want immediate deterministic switch. Perhaps a two-tier system: kill-switch (hard threshold) + soft-arbiter (probabilistic) for intermediate cases.

nisha: Agreed. Hard thresholds: policy_score>=90 -> immediate switch. For 60-90 -> arbiter chooses X% of candidates proportional to policy_score and tenant_risk. Lower scores -> noop or drain only.

tom: How to surface this in telemetry? We need clear metrics: fallback.policy_score, fallback.arbiter.selection_pct, fallback.leash.engaged, fallback.hard_triggers.count. Also audit events.

nisha: Proposed audit fields: decision_id, applied_action, arbiter_path (hard|probabilistic|manual), policy_score, tenant_risk, trace_id. Emit fallback.audit.log_written when we persist the decision.

eli: Operator runbook snippet: if many probabilistic selections are firing and aborts spike, temporarily turn arbiter into deterministic mode (toggle arbiter.mode=deterministic) and increase suppress_window_s. Add snippet to toggle via ops API.

ops-bot: ops: flag updated in staging: arbiter.mode=probabilistic default, suppress_window_s=120.

tom: Need Decision API shape (flat): decision_id, service, route, trigger_ts, evaluated_at, ttl_s, action, target, policy_score, arbiter_path, provenance_str, decision_state, attempt, trace_id, request_hash, signals="latency_p95=...;err_pct=...;quality_drop=..."

nisha: I'll add that. Also add a reconciliation mechanism: every decision is appended to decisions log; reconciler checks for conflicting decisions for same service+route within reconcile_window_s and emits fallback.reconcile.attempt & fallback.reconcile.resolution. If conflict can't be resolved, mark decision_state=aborted and page infra.

eli: Good. Also enforce idempotency by decision_id and include decision_signature (HMAC) to prevent tampering when ops override via external tools. Record fallback.audit.log_written with signature field.

tom: Ops toggle snippet for runbook:```bash
# toggle arbiter mode
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"arbiter.mode":"deterministic"}' \
  https://ops-api.internal.redwood/internal/arbiter/config
```

nisha: Alert rules: page infra if fallback.reconcile.resolution==conflict AND reconcile.attempts>1 in 10m. Page also if fallback.hard_triggers.count spikes. Lower-sev for many probabilistic selections without applied actions.

eli: I'll own reconciler and signature checks. Tom can you add the metrics+dashboards?

tom: Yep, will add panels for policy_score distributions and arbiter selection_pct.

nisha: Great. I'll draft the runbook with the API shapes and example payloads and PR to runbooks repo. Will link here when up. :thumbsup:
